Extract group-level estimates of random effects

Source: R/pglmm-ranef.R
ranef.Rd

Extract group-level estimates of random effects

Usage

# S3 method for class 'communityPGLMM'
ranef(object, condVar = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'ranef.pglmm'
print(x, n = 10L, ...)

Arguments

object

A fitted model with class communityPGLMM.

condVar

Whether to also return the conditional standard deviations of the estimates (column se), calculated conditional on the estimated fixed effects and variances of random terms, as in lme4. They are therefore smaller than those of glmmTMB::ranef(condVar = TRUE), which also include the uncertainty of these estimates. Only used when bayes = FALSE. This needs more computation than the estimates themselves for large data sets. Default is FALSE.

...

Ignored.

x

Output of ranef().

n

Number of rows to print for each random term.

Value

A named list with one data frame for each random term, in the same order as the random terms of the model. Each data frame has one row per level, with one or two columns to identify the level (named after the grouping variables), and a column estimate. For bayes = FALSE and condVar = TRUE, there is also a column se. For bayes = TRUE, there are also columns sd, lower and upper (posterior standard deviation and 95% credible interval).

Details

Extract the estimates of each level of each random term (e.g. one value per species for (1 | sp)) from a fitted model, similar to lme4::ranef(). To get the variances of the random terms, use VarCorr().

For models fitted by maximum likelihood (bayes = FALSE), the estimates are the conditional modes (BLUPs) of the random effects given the data and the estimated parameters, \(\hat{u}_k = \sigma_k^2 C_k Z_k' V^{-1} (y - X\beta)\). For binomial and poisson models fitted with method = "PQL", they are the conditional modes of the penalized quasi-likelihood (PQL) fit, calculated with the working response; they will be close to, but not the same as, the estimates from models fitted with a Laplace approximation (e.g. lme4::glmer(), glmmTMB::glmmTMB()). With method = "Laplace", they are the conditional modes of the Laplace approximation (the same as those of glmer() and glmmTMB()), and their conditional standard deviations are from its Hessian. For Bayesian models (bayes = TRUE), the estimates are summaries of the posterior marginal distributions of the latent random effects.

All estimates are on the scale of the linear predictor. They do not depend on the standardization of the covariance matrices (e.g. to have determinant of one), because the estimated variance of the random term absorbs it.

A phylogenetic term such as (1 | sp__) is fitted as two random terms (see pglmm()): a non-phylogenetic one (1|sp) and a phylogenetic one (1|sp__). They are reported separately; their sum is the total effect of a species.

Nested terms such as (1 | sp__@site) have one value for every combination of the two grouping variables that was observed in the data. Only the levels that appear in the data have an estimate (e.g. not the species that are in the phylogeny but not in the data). Note that the levels are in the order of their first appearance in the data, not sorted alphabetically as in lme4.

See also

VarCorr() for the variances of random terms.

Examples

# community data: abundance of each species at each site
dat <- data.frame(
  site = rep(rownames(comm_a), times = ncol(comm_a)),
  sp = rep(colnames(comm_a), each = nrow(comm_a)),
  freq = unlist(comm_a, use.names = FALSE)
)
dat$shade <- envi$shade[match(dat$site, envi$site)]
phy <- ape::keep.tip(phylotree, unique(dat$sp))
fit <- pglmm(freq ~ shade + (1 | sp__) + (1 | site),
  data = dat, cov_ranef = list(sp = phy)
)
#> boundary (singular) fit: the variances of 1|sp, 1|site are (close to) zero; see ?pglmm_is_singular

# one data frame for each random term; (1 | sp__) is fitted as two terms
re <- ranef(fit)
names(re)
#> [1] "1|sp"   "1|sp__" "1|site"
re
#> $`1|sp`
#>                           sp estimate
#> 1                Acer_rubrum        0
#> 2       Achillea_millefolium        0
#> 3            Amelanchier_spp        0
#> 4        Andropogon_gerardii        0
#> 5       Anemone_quinquefolia        0
#> 6  Apocynum_androsaemifolium        0
#> 7       Aquilegia_canadensis        0
#> 8          Aralia_nudicaulis        0
#> 9          Betula_papyrifera        0
#> 10      Chimaphila_umbellata        0
#> # ... 5 more rows
#> 
#> $`1|sp__`
#>                           sp    estimate
#> 1                Acer_rubrum  2.68283138
#> 2       Achillea_millefolium -0.22365137
#> 3            Amelanchier_spp  0.04192377
#> 4        Andropogon_gerardii -0.34587015
#> 5       Anemone_quinquefolia -0.46194139
#> 6  Apocynum_androsaemifolium  0.55004997
#> 7       Aquilegia_canadensis -0.51448613
#> 8          Aralia_nudicaulis  0.69886492
#> 9          Betula_papyrifera -0.20822827
#> 10      Chimaphila_umbellata -0.51091584
#> # ... 5 more rows
#> 
#> $`1|site`
#>     site estimate
#> 1  s3293        0
#> 2  s3294        0
#> 3  s3295        0
#> 4  s3296        0
#> 5  s3297        0
#> 6  s3299        0
#> 7  s3300        0
#> 8  s3301        0
#> 9  s3302        0
#> 10 s3303        0
#> # ... 5 more rows
#> 
head(re[["1|sp__"]])
#>                          sp    estimate
#> 1               Acer_rubrum  2.68283138
#> 2      Achillea_millefolium -0.22365137
#> 3           Amelanchier_spp  0.04192377
#> 4       Andropogon_gerardii -0.34587015
#> 5      Anemone_quinquefolia -0.46194139
#> 6 Apocynum_androsaemifolium  0.55004997

# total effect of each species: non-phylogenetic plus phylogenetic
data.frame(
  sp = re[["1|sp"]]$sp,
  estimate = re[["1|sp"]]$estimate + re[["1|sp__"]]$estimate
)
#>                           sp    estimate
#> 1                Acer_rubrum  2.68283138
#> 2       Achillea_millefolium -0.22365137
#> 3            Amelanchier_spp  0.04192377
#> 4        Andropogon_gerardii -0.34587015
#> 5       Anemone_quinquefolia -0.46194139
#> 6  Apocynum_androsaemifolium  0.55004997
#> 7       Aquilegia_canadensis -0.51448613
#> 8          Aralia_nudicaulis  0.69886492
#> 9          Betula_papyrifera -0.20822827
#> 10      Chimaphila_umbellata -0.51091584

#> 12        Comandra_umbellata -0.52051336
#> 13       Comptonia_peregrina  0.23506938
#> 14         Cornus_canadensis  0.01801886
#> 15         Corylus_americana -0.09292072

# with conditional standard deviations of the estimates
head(ranef(fit, condVar = TRUE)[["1|sp__"]])
#>                          sp    estimate        se
#> 1               Acer_rubrum  2.68283138 0.4197741
#> 2      Achillea_millefolium -0.22365137 0.4196879
#> 3           Amelanchier_spp  0.04192377 0.4152745
#> 4       Andropogon_gerardii -0.34587015 0.4268867
#> 5      Anemone_quinquefolia -0.46194139 0.3766951
#> 6 Apocynum_androsaemifolium  0.55004997 0.4208974

# variances of the random terms
VarCorr(fit)
#>           Variance   Std.Dev
#> 1|sp     0.0000000 0.0000000
#> 1|sp__   0.7748109 0.8802334
#> 1|site   0.0000000 0.0000000
#> residual 3.2656287 1.8071051
